findings: Freshly retrieved adopted 2026–2027 Appendix I has the same SHA256 as the version inspected for CP223. Its English track table independently confirms all twenty-eight components. The current programme page expressly identifies September 2026–2027 and agrees on thirteen first-year units totalling sixty EC, ten six-credit second-year units, and the thirty-credit mobility window plus eighteen taught credits and twelve-credit thesis.

The exact English track differs from Dutch Personeelwetenschappen: Sociology of Work, Organizational Psychology for People Management and Strategic Management for People Management appear in year one; Talent Management replaces the Dutch personnel-assessment unit. The final year requires Comparative Labor Relations in Europe, Social Philosophy for People Management and Cross-Cultural HRM. The current exact-target page explains talent as hiring, development, careers and measurement; cross-cultural HRM concerns selection, involvement, development, inclusion and international teamwork. These differences inform the UCR contribution assessment.

General OER 4.5 requires 120 earned credits for bachelor thesis entry. The track-specific appendix gives no additional thesis entry condition. Completing years one and two meets the threshold. General OER 4.4 concerns later assessments for postponed BSA students, requiring permission or forty-two credits, and 5.6 sets the ordinary forty-two-credit positive BSA threshold. Practical-exercise participation applies to marked units. GROW mentoring and development is zero credit and is not counted within 180.

The adopted appendix permits thirty EC of placement, minor and/or free electives, at home or abroad; it refers specific combinations to the catalogue. The comparison preserves the approved open window without selecting a placement or combination, promising a particular allocation or inventing subject content. The public page illustrates full-window exchange, internship and minor choices. No arbitrary extra course is selected to close credits.
